strings.name: Faith Kipyegon
strings.summary: Faith Kipyegon is a Kenyan middle-distance runner who progressed from barefoot junior cross-country racing to world-class 1500m competition. She won consecutive Olympic 1500m golds in 2016, Tokyo 2020 and 2024, and the 1500m and 5000m at the 2023 World Championships. In 2025 she improved the 1500m world record to 3:48.68 and won her fourth outdoor world title at the distance, before exploring longer road races.

strings.influence.rationale: Her Olympic titles and middle-distance world records have increased the international influence of African women’s athletics.

strings.highlights.olympic.title: Three consecutive Olympic 1500m golds
strings.highlights.olympic.text: She won in Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, making women’s Olympic 1500m history.
strings.highlights.record.title: 1500m world record
strings.highlights.record.text: Her 3:48.68 in Eugene on 5 July 2025 was ratified by World Athletics that September.
strings.timeline.road26.title: Road 10km debut
strings.timeline.road26.text: She won her first road 10km in Monaco in 29:46, extending her competition to a longer distance.
strings.timeline.world25.title: Fourth outdoor world 1500m title
strings.timeline.world25.text: She won the women’s 1500m in Tokyo; as of that race her four titles came in 2017, 2022, 2023 and 2025.
strings.timeline.record25.title: Under 3:49
strings.timeline.record25.text: In Eugene she lowered the 1500m world record to 3:48.68, improving her 2024 mark by 0.36 seconds.
strings.timeline.paris24.title: Olympic three-peat in Paris
strings.timeline.paris24.text: She set an Olympic record of 3:51.29 and won a third consecutive women’s 1500m gold.
strings.timeline.double23.title: Budapest double
strings.timeline.double23.text: She won both the 1500m and 5000m at the same outdoor World Championships, showing her range across middle and long distances.
strings.timeline.world22.title: Regained the world title
strings.timeline.world22.text: She won her second outdoor world 1500m title in Oregon, following her first in 2017.
strings.timeline.rio16.title: Olympic gold in Rio
strings.timeline.rio16.text: She won women’s 1500m gold in Rio de Janeiro, beginning her run of consecutive Olympic titles in the event.
strings.timeline.junior12.title: World junior 1500m champion
strings.timeline.junior12.text: She won the world junior 1500m title in Barcelona, building on her breakthrough at the 2011 world youth championships.
strings.timeline.debut10.title: Barefoot international debut
strings.timeline.debut10.text: At 16 she raced barefoot at the World Cross Country Championships in Poland, finishing fourth in the U20 race and entering international competition.
